title: Judgment-point registry (llm-points) v1
description: One entry per place in a system where a model is asked to decide or produce something (a judgment point): who calls it, what it does, what the output looks like, and what happens when the model does not answer or the output is invalid. Two systems share this format; each keeps its own registry contents. Shared fields: caller, purpose, output, on_failure; every other field is used by one side only and is optional. Unknown fields are rejected at the point level: to add a field, change this schema first and have the other side sync its copy the same day before using it. Adding a field does not bump the version; renaming a field or changing its meaning does.

points.description: Point name → declaration. Names are lowercase letters and digits, with - or _.

exempt.description: Calls that temporarily bypass the registry (each with a reason)

caller.description: Who makes the request (file or module)

schema.description: The output's JSON Schema file (relative to the registry file's directory); only when format is json

on_failure.description: What actually happens when the model does not answer or its output is invalid (there is no "silently use another model or another result" option): skip = skip this time, keep no result; retry_later = do not advance progress, try again next round; ask_user = ask the user instead; say_so = tell the user (or the status page / an alert) plainly that the model did not answer; default = use a safe result declared in advance (the value can be in the default field, or supplied by the caller)

default.description: The safe result when on_failure is default and the registry supplies it; if this field is present, a failure returns this value

kind.description: decide = pick one of a fixed set of conclusions (could be replaced by a classifier that returns probabilities); generate = produce content

labels.description: The conclusions a decide point can return

model_group.description: The group name when models are chosen by group (e.g. fast / standard / strong; default = unspecified, the tool's own default)

shape.description: completion = the model has no tools and only answers (any LLM provider can run it); agent = a coding agent that needs tools, a working directory and permissions (docs/design/llm-providers.md)

max_attempts.description: The most requests one completion call may make, every retry counted (rate limits, an invalid answer asked again); 1 = no retry. Default: the implementation's own retries

material.description: What kind of material is sent to the model (decides whether it may go to the cloud)

scorer.description: How it is scored; judge = a model acts as judge

truth.description: Where the correct answer comes from

model_env.description: Read the model name from this environment variable

prompts.description: Who answers permission prompts; none = always deny

restricted.description: no settings file is loaded; a runtime that can't be told (no confined runs) may run the point only in the platform's throwaway copy, otherwise the run fails saying so (llm.py), and doctor says what that leaves

works_in.description: Its folder is a copy of a project's memory branch: the platform checks the files before the run, on every runtime, and refuses one that holds more than notes (a folder that passes doesn't need the throwaway copy restricted otherwise asks of a runtime with no confined runs)

tools.description: Tools it may use (comma-separated; empty string = all off)

allowed_tools.description: Permission rules that are allowed automatically

extra_allow_env.description: Extra allow rules the caller adds through this environment variable (a JSON list; adds rules, does not change the mode)

allow_from_env.description: Unattended: when this environment variable is set, only those rules are allowed and everything else is denied

tool_servers.description: When the run loads the tool servers configured in its environment, deny each one whose tools its allow list doesn't name (found by the runtime for that run; when it can't be told, the run doesn't happen)

settings.description: platform = load none of the user's, the project's or local tool settings: only the platform's own for the project named by the project_env variable (its sandbox when enforced, its deny list, the platform's commands), so the declared rules are the whole boundary

project_env.description: The environment variable that names the run's project: required with settings: platform; on another point, a sandboxed project's run is refused

stream.description: A long-running streaming session (not one question, one answer)
